chunks: Then after affliction He sent you a drowsiness, a sleep that overcame some of you, while another group was anxious for themselves, thinking thoughts of pagan ignorance; they said, 'Do we have any say in the matter?' Say, 'All affairs belong to God.' They hide in their hearts what they do not disclose to you. They say, 'If we had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here.' Tell them, 'Even if you had stayed at home, those who were ordained to be killed would have gone to their places of rest, so that God might test what is in your breasts and purify what is in your hearts, and God is Knower of that within the breasts.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the drowsiness and anxiety of the believers during the Battle of Uhud?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is pivotal for understanding the spiritual trial of the Muhajirun and Ansar during Uhud, where the 'sleep' of some and the 'anxiety' of others both served to purify the believers' hearts (tazkiyah) and expose hidden hypocrisies. It highlights the transition from the fatalistic 'Jahiliyyah' view of fate to the Islamic conviction that all outcomes are decreed by Allah, reinforcing the concept of divine testing (ibtala') for spiritual refinement.
